slides.caption: Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin shook hands in China ahead of an unprecedented three-way summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping. Officials rolled out a red carpet for the gathering in Shenzhen, which marked the first meeting between Trump and Putin in over a year.

slides.caption: The International Court of Justice is preparing to deliver its ruling in a seven-year-old genocide lawsuit brought against Myanmar by The Gambia. A conviction would mark the first time in history that a sovereign state has been found guilty of genocide by an international court.

slides.caption: Israeli ground forces and tanks advanced east of the Nuseirat refugee camp into territory outside their control following evacuation orders. The rare military advance beyond the Yellow Line was accompanied by heavy artillery strikes near both Nuseirat and Bureij camps.

slides.caption: Artificial intelligence developer Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 per share, surpassing its projected range of $70 to $78. The blockbuster pricing gives the company a fully diluted market valuation of $1.5 trillion ahead of trading on the Nasdaq.

slides.caption: Leading financial institutions including Citibank have updated their terms of service to deny responsibility for unauthorized transactions caused by third-party artificial intelligence assistants. Customers who grant automated tools access to their accounts will bear all financial liabilities even when stolen funds result from a hack.

slides.headline: GERMAN JUDGE OFFERS TO DROP CRIMINAL PIRACY CASE FOR **BILLIONS IN BITCOIN**
slides.caption: A German judge proposed dismissing the criminal proceedings against the operator of piracy portal Movie2k if the defendant surrenders $2.56 billion worth of bitcoin. The suggested agreement would close the legal prosecution tied to one of the largest copyright infringement networks in Germany.

slides.caption: Microsoft chief executive Satya Nadella warned at the DealBook Summit that vital infrastructure across the globe contains unfixable software flaws. He emphasized that internet-linked equipment like data center chillers, HVAC units, and firmware cannot be patched against artificial intelligence cyberthreats.
